entities.name: Gaius Caninius Rebilus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gaius Caninius Rebilus was a Roman senator who was appointed suffect consul in 12 BC with Lucius Volusius Saturninus as his colleague.

Rebilus was born in Italy, but his origins are unclear. As a member of the Roman Senate, he played a significant role in the governance of Rome during the late Republic.

His appointment as suffect consul marked a turning point in the tumultuous politics of the time, as he worked alongside Volusius Saturninus to maintain order and stability in the empire.

Rebilus's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he was a key figure in the rise of the Julio-Claudian dynasty, which would go on to shape the course of Roman history.

"The fate of the Roman Republic hangs in the balance, and the actions of men like Rebilus will determine its future."
